title: Open administration screens using the current hash routes
prerequisites: An authenticated Claims UI session for guarded administration screens.
The organization's configured menu and action access; no universal menu hierarchy is established by these sources.
steps: Use the application URL followed by # and the relative route, for example #/usermanagement/userprofile.
For editing users, organizations, rules or tasks, open the relevant list and use its New, Add New, Edit or View action rather than opening a detail route without navigation state.
If a guarded screen is unavailable, have an authorized administrator review configured menu access and the current session instead of assuming that knowing the URL grants access.
notes: The settings module is mounted at /usermanagement, not /settings. Rules and tasks have their own mounts.

AuthGuard validates the session and configured menu URLs; it explicitly omits some routes from menu matching, including task/rules routes and dashboard/profile routes. This is not a statement of backend authorization.
/workflow-status is a separate top-level token-link screen, not a settings child.
These are source-verified instructions, not a live-environment execution test. Feature availability and returned lookup choices are role/configuration conditional.

title: Find a user and inspect the vacation indicator
prerequisites: Access to User Profile Management and the applicable View/Edit/New actions.
steps: Open /usermanagement/userprofile and use the grid's search, ordering and paging controls to locate a user.
Review Name, Login Id, Email, Mobile, Address and Status to distinguish the intended record.
Use the eye action to view or the pencil action to edit where available.
When the vacation indicator is shown, open it to inspect Vacation Details and Vacation Period; use Close to dismiss the popup.
notes: Edit action visibility is conditional on the access information passed to the list.
The vacation popup is informational; it does not itself create or modify a vacation.
Do not paste personal user details or actual vacation records into AI requests.

title: Create a user profile
prerequisites: New-user access and configured organization roles/reporting supervisors.
Open the form using the list's add action; the detail component expects history state.
steps: From the user list, use the add action to open User Profile Management.
On User Profile, enter Name, Email ID, Login ID, Password, Password Valid To, Mobile Number and Address.
Choose Organization Role, then choose Reporting Supervisor from the role-dependent list.
Set Active and Is Excluded Task Management deliberately; enter User Name Arabic if needed.
Use Save and review the returned message. A successful response returns to the user list.
To configure Roles and Special Authorization, reopen the saved user: Role/Access is disabled for a new unsaved user.
notes: Name, Login ID, Password, Password Valid To, Email ID, Mobile Number, Address, Organization Role and Reporting Supervisor have required validators.
Email must be valid; Mobile Number must contain 10–13 digits. Template limits include Name 200, User Name Arabic 500 and Address 300 characters.
Active and exclusion flags are saved, but their complete downstream effects are not proven by this form alone.
No password value or credential example is included in this knowledge.

title: Change a user's organization role or reporting supervisor
prerequisites: An existing user opened with the list's Edit action.
Any required task reassignment coordinated by an authorized task administrator.
steps: Open the user's pencil action and review the existing Organization Role and Reporting Supervisor.
Change Organization Role first when necessary so that the reporting-supervisor choices reload.
Select the appropriate Reporting Supervisor, update other editable required fields and use Save.

If Cannot Save reports pending tasks for the current organization role and supervisor, stop the role/supervisor change and coordinate task resolution or reassignment; retry only after the underlying condition has changed.
After a successful save, verify the record again from the user list.
notes: Login ID and Password are disabled when an existing user is loaded; this screen is not a verified password-reset workflow.
The frontend checks the original role/supervisor combination before saving a changed combination.

Despite the pending-tasks wording, the inspected repository check tests active task membership under an active task master for technical or medical reviewers; it does not inspect claim completion status in that check.
The user-form Delete handler only displays an alert; do not describe it as a working user deletion feature.

title: Assign roles and special authorization to an existing user
prerequisites: A saved user opened in Edit mode.
Configured roles and authorization lookup values.
steps: Open the existing user and select Role/Access.
Use Roles to select or deselect the required roles.
Review the Access section after role changes; role selection reloads the menu/action access associated with the selected roles.
Choose applicable Special Authorization entries from Authorization.
Use Save and verify the returned result, then reopen the user to confirm selections.
notes: Role/Access is enabled only for existing users.
The current template applies pointer-events: none to the Access section. Treat it as a role-derived access preview, not a verified directly editable per-user permission matrix.
Organization Role on User Profile is distinct from the multiselect Roles on Role/Access.
Role and authorization changes do not prove immediate session/menu refresh for the affected user; refresh behavior must be verified in the target environment.

title: Record a user vacation
prerequisites: Access to User Vacation and its add action.
An existing user available in the user lookup.
steps: Open /usermanagement/uservacation and use the add action.
Choose the user, Start Date and End Date; these fields are required.
Set Active as intended and use Save.
Review the server response. A successful result returns to the vacation list.
If saving is blocked with the pending/error-claims message, coordinate with task administrators to resolve the underlying assignments before trying again.
notes: The user lookup displays a user name together with the login identifier; do not copy actual values into AI requests.
Date pickers use DD/MM/YYYY and have today's date as their minimum selectable date.
The backend derives the organization and acting user from context; the list is scoped to the current organization.

The backend can reject a vacation with 'User has pending or error status claims within the selected period. Vacation cannot be saved.' Its inspected date predicate is not a conventional complete range-overlap test, so do not promise precisely which claims will block each date range.
Required-date controls do not establish comprehensive server-side start/end chronology or overlap validation.

title: Review or edit an existing vacation and understand locked dates
prerequisites: An existing vacation opened through its pencil or eye action.
steps: Find the vacation in the list using User Name, Login Id, Start Date, End Date and Status.
Use the eye to review or pencil to edit.
If today's date falls between the loaded start and end dates inclusive, expect Start Date and End Date to be disabled.
Where editing is permitted, update the user, unlocked dates or active flag as appropriate, then use Save and inspect the returned result.
Use Back to return to the list without asserting a save occurred.
notes: Loaded dd/MM/yyyy dates are parsed before the current-period check; the save uses raw values so disabled date fields remain in the payload.
The loaded-period check is based on calendar dates, independently of the Is Active flag.
The form's Delete handler is not implemented. Although a deactivation endpoint exists, the inspected list exposes edit/view, not a separate verified deactivation button.
The date-check method can re-enable dates outside the current period after loading; treat View as a review workflow and do not infer server-side enforcement from disabled controls.

title: Update your own profile and sign in again
prerequisites: An authenticated session with a loaded current-user profile.
steps: Open /usermanagement/update-profile.
Update Name, Name in Arabic, Email and Phone as appropriate.
Keep Name, a valid Email and a 10–13 digit numeric Phone populated.
For a profile-only change, leave both password fields empty.
Use Save when enabled. On a successful response, acknowledge the message asking you to log in again; the component logs out the session.
notes: Save is disabled while loading or when the form is pristine or invalid.
Although the template marks Name in Arabic with an asterisk, the inspected form does not give it a required validator.
The profile component also holds an address control; do not assume an address input is visible merely from that model control.

title: Change your password from Update Profile
prerequisites: An authenticated current-user session.
A new password selected privately, never supplied to an AI assistant.
steps: Open Update Profile and ensure Name, Email and Phone remain valid.
Enter the new value in Password and repeat the same value in Retype Password.
Use a value satisfying the coded pattern: 5–15 characters with at least one lowercase letter, one digit and one of ! @ # $ % ^ &.
Use Save; correct 'Passwords doesn't match' if the two entries differ.
After a successful update, acknowledge the prompt and sign in again.
notes: Password fields are optional when both are empty.

The current component installs its password validators when the value length becomes one and removes them when empty. Validation of pasted or programmatically populated values is not proven to follow the same path; the stated pattern is the coded rule, not a guarantee of every input path.
This changes the current user's profile password; no administrator reset-password action was verified in these scoped screens.

title: Create a role in Role Setup
prerequisites: Access to Role Setup and the New action.
steps: Open /usermanagement/rolesetup and use the New control beside Roles.
Enter a nonblank Role Name.
Optionally enter Role Name in Arabic and Description.
Use the dialog's save button and inspect the returned success or error message.
Select the role in the Roles list before configuring its menu/action access.
notes: Role Name is required and limited to 80 characters; a whitespace-only name is rejected.
Role Name in Arabic is limited to 80 characters and Description to 200.
Creating a role does not itself assign it to users; use the existing user's Role/Access tab separately.

title: Save a role's menu and action permissions
prerequisites: An existing role and edit access to the role-access screen.
Modules, menus and actions already configured.
steps: Select the intended role in Roles to load its current module, menu and action mappings.
For each intended menu, select or clear the relevant action checkboxes; a menu-level checkbox applies its state to that menu's mapped actions.
Review the menu state after changing individual actions: it reflects whether at least one action is enabled.
Use the screen's Save action.
If 'There are no changes to save' appears, make an actual intended checkbox change rather than assuming a save occurred; reload the role to verify stored access.
notes: Permission availability is configuration-dependent; these sources do not establish a universal administrator role name.
Role access is saved through UpsertAssignRole, independently of the role-creation dialog.
Access changes in a role are not evidence that an already signed-in user's menu is immediately rebuilt.

title: Add a module master in Module Management
prerequisites: Access to Module Management and the configured creation action.
An approved module definition; this is configuration rather than normal claims processing.
steps: Open /usermanagement/rcmmapping.
Use Add Module from Module List where the control is available.
Enter the module name and any applicable Arabic name or description.
Use SAVE and review the refreshed Module List.
Select the module to inspect its Menu Details.
notes: The module name is required and must be 6–30 characters; Arabic name and description are not required by the inspected form.
Saving a module master does not create an Angular route, backend endpoint or user permission automatically.
This component derives its creation visibility from configured action access; do not infer that every signed-in user can maintain masters.

title: Add an action master for menu configuration
prerequisites: Authorized access to Module Management and the Add Action control.
steps: Open Module Management and use Add Action from Action List.
Populate the action name and Arabic action name; both are required by the form.
Enter an action description if applicable.
Use SAVE and review the refreshed master-action choices.
Associate the action with the appropriate menu using Add Menu or Edit Menu rather than assuming the master alone grants access.
notes: Action masters, menu/action associations, role grants and user-role assignments are separate configuration operations.
No business behavior is created solely by adding a named action; consumers must already recognize the action.

title: Add or edit a module's menu and associated actions
prerequisites: An existing module and action masters.
Authorized access to the applicable menu-configuration controls.
steps: Select a module from Module List to load Menu Details.
Use View Details to inspect an existing menu's action list without assuming it saves changes.
Use Add Menu or Edit Menu for an intended configuration change.
Enter a valid menu name, set any displayed Arabic name, remarks, image/tooltip and active state, and select the intended Action checkboxes.
Use SAVE and inspect the refreshed menu list for the selected module.
notes: The menu-name validator requires 6–30 characters and permits alphabetic words separated by spaces, not arbitrary punctuation or digits.
The menu payload contains the selected module and accumulated action selections.
Do not invent a URL or claim a new menu makes an unimplemented feature reachable; route creation is outside this form.

title: Create an organization from Organization Setup
prerequisites: Organization Setup access with the New action.
Country, state and city lookup data.
steps: Open /usermanagement/organization-setup and use the add action.
Enter Organization Name and Organization Name Arabic.
Choose Country, then State, then City; changing a parent location clears dependent choices.
Enter Phone Office 1 and any appropriate Email Address, WebSite Url, address, registration or tax-registration information.
Set Active deliberately and use Save.
Review the returned message; a successful result navigates back to Organization Setup.
notes: Both organization names, Country, State, City and Phone Office 1 are required.
Email is validated when supplied. Phone Office 1 requires 10–13 digits; optional Phone Office 2 and Fax No have the same length/digit restrictions.
Optional Zip Code requires 5–10 digits when populated; WebSite Url has a URL-pattern validator.
Open the detail form through the list because it expects organization ID and edit/view mode in history state.

title: Edit organization details and choose an organization logo
prerequisites: An existing organization opened from the list's pencil action.
steps: Find the organization using the searchable list's Organization Name, Web Site Url, Email Address and Status.
Use Edit for changes or View for review.
Update the permitted contact, location or active-state fields, keeping required values valid.
Under Organization Logo, use Choose file and inspect the preview and displayed filename.
If needed, use Remove to clear the local preview, then Save and reopen the organization to verify the persisted result.
notes: Organization Name and Organization Name Arabic are disabled for existing organizations.
The logo picker accepts image files and its hint says JPG, PNG. Selected logo data is read as a data URL; the inspected handler establishes no file-size validation.

Remove clears the form's logo and local preview, but saving merges form data into an existing object and conditionally reassigns logo data. Verify actual server-side removal after saving; do not promise deletion from the preview alone.
No separate working organization deletion workflow is established by the inspected sources.

title: Create or edit a User Notification Group
prerequisites: Access to User Notification Group and available user choices.
steps: Open /usermanagement/usernotificationgroup.
For a new group, enter Group Name and select at least one entry in Users.
Use Save and review the returned message and refreshed group list.
To modify an existing group, use its pencil action; review Group Name and Users, then Save.
Use Cancel while editing to clear the edit context and return to new-group entry.
notes: Group Name and Users have required validators; Save is disabled while the form is invalid. The Group Name input is limited to 15 characters.
The list shows Group Name and Users Count.
A client-side duplicate-name warning exists, but its lookup uses a differently cased property than the displayed data. Do not promise complete uniqueness enforcement based on the client check.
This screen maintains recipient groups; it does not itself demonstrate sending a notification.

title: Choose dashboard tiles and graph previews for a role
prerequisites: Dashboard Setup access and applicable New or Edit action permission.
An existing role.
steps: Open Dashboard Setup and select a value in Roles; the role is required.
Wait for the role's saved setup to load, or for default unselected widgets if no setup exists.
Click the intended information tiles and graph previews; check overlays indicate selected items.
Use Save for a new setup or Update for an existing setup when the button is enabled.
Review the server response and reselect the role to check the stored configuration.
notes: The configured tile components are Received, Un-Claimed, Claimed, Accepted and Rejected; the current template incorrectly labels the fifth tile 'Received'. Use position and styling cautiously rather than assuming both labels represent the same widget.
Two graph-preview toggles exist: the claim-stages summary and the second financial/facility preview.
Save/Update is disabled when loading, pristine or invalid, and visibility is action-permission conditional.
The payload stores component visibility/order JSON by RoleId; no drag-to-reorder workflow is visible in this template.

title: Filter facilities and enable or disable their AI agent
prerequisites: Configured access to the AI Assistant Configuration route.
Organization and facility lookup services available.
steps: Open /usermanagement/ai-assistant-config.
Choose an Organization or All Organizations, then a Facility or All Facilities.
Review Organization, Facility and AI Agent Status in the matching rows.
Use Enable for a disabled facility or Disable for an enabled facility.
Wait for the update to finish and inspect the status and result message before making another change.
notes: Changing Organization clears the selected Facility and restricts its dropdown choices.
All action buttons are disabled while an update is in progress.
The component changes the displayed state only when the response Status is true and otherwise displays an error.

This is a facility AI-agent flag, not proof that the AI API has loaded knowledge articles, that the chat interface is deployed or that every AI feature is enabled. Backend flag behavior beyond the inspected service call is unverified.

title: Create or edit a rule group with payer and event associations
prerequisites: Rule Group Management access and applicable New/Edit controls.
Existing payer and event lookup values.
steps: Open /usermanagement/rulegroupmanagement.
Use the plus action on Rule Group List to create a group, or the group's edit action to modify it.
Enter Rule Group Name and Entity Name, and select Events and Payers.
Enter Remarks if needed and set Is Active.
Use the dialog's save action and inspect the result; reopen the group to verify its associations.
notes: Rule Group Name, Entity Name, Events and Payers are required by the current form.
The payload contains one rule-group detail object plus payer-ID and event-ID lists.
The save finalizer refreshes and closes the dialog even when the response reports failure; closing is not proof of persistence.
This association workflow is distinct from configuring which fields belong to the group and from authoring a rule expression.

title: Add, remove or reactivate fields available to a rule group
prerequisites: An existing rule group and field-parameter lookup data.
Permission to save rule-group configuration.
steps: Select the intended group from Rule Group List.
In Rule Group Configuration, choose the available fields and use the plus action to add them to the group's grid.
Review Field Name, Remarks and Status.
Use the row's Remove action to mark a field inactive, or Add to reactivate it.
Use the page save action for the field configuration, then select the group again to confirm stored state.
notes: The component rejects adding/saving field configuration without a selected rule group.
Adding an already present field reactivates it rather than inserting another client-side entry.
Row Remove toggles IsActive locally; persistence requires saving the selectedRuleFields collection.
Field choices in rule builders depend on group configuration; do not invent a field absent from the returned lookup.
The related backend SaveRuleGroupFields endpoint requires the Rule_Field_Mapping Edit action; the configured policy determines actual access.

title: Maintain a payer, event and rule-group mapping
prerequisites: Configured payer, event and rule group.
Access to the mapping list and applicable Add/Edit/View action.
steps: Open /usermanagement/payerrulemapping and search the grid by the displayed Payer Name, Entity Name, Event Name, Rule Group or Status.
Use the add action for a new mapping, pencil to edit or eye to review.
Enter a nonblank Entity Name and select Payer, Event and Rule Group.
Set Is Active as appropriate, then use Save.
Use Back and reload the list to verify the mapping.
notes: EntityName, PayerId, EventId and RuleGroupId are required; whitespace-only Entity Name is explicitly rejected.
Open the detail screen through list navigation, which supplies the mapping ID and allowEdit flag.
The current save handler shows 'Payer event rule saved.' for an HTTP success without checking response Status. Verify the record rather than treating that toast alone as persistence proof.
This single-payer mapping form coexists with the multi-payer/event rule-group dialog; do not assume their duplicate handling or downstream execution priority.

title: Find rules in the settings Rules screen
prerequisites: Access to the settings Rules screen and configured rule groups.
steps: Open /usermanagement/rule.
Choose a group in Select Rule Group, or ALL to request all rules.
Use the grid's search and ordering controls to inspect Group Name, Rule Name, Expression, Result, Exe.Order and IsActive.
Use the add action for a new rule, pencil to edit or eye to view; these actions open /usermanagement/managerule with the required navigation state.
notes: The settings rule editor is a separate routed component from /rules/manage-rule.
Do not substitute one editor's result-column labels or Type field for the other; the settings editor lacks the newer Type and Attach To Field controls.
Action availability depends on the configured access state.

title: Author a rule in the settings rule editor
prerequisites: Open the settings editor using Add or Edit from /usermanagement/rule.
A configured rule group with applicable fields and user functions.
steps: Select Rule Group and enter Rule Name, Rule Description and ExecOrder; set Active deliberately.
In Rule Expressions, select Field, Operator and Value and use the displayed bracket, UserFunc and Arithmetic controls only as needed.
Select AND or OR in Condition before adding another expression row.
In Results, enter Result Name and Result Value, then select Severity Level and Severity Category.
Check the generated Expression text, balance opening/closing brackets and correct any reported RegularExp error.
Use Save and then reload the settings rule list to confirm the stored result.
notes: Rule Name, Rule Description and ExecOrder have required validators; expression Field/Operator/Value and result name/value/severity controls also carry required validators.
Save explicitly rejects a missing group, missing or whitespace-only name, unbalanced bracket counts and a flagged invalid regular expression.
Only the last remaining expression/result row cannot be removed.
Available field, function and severity choices come from services. Hidden/commented create-group controls are not a verified normal entry path; use Rule Group Management.
This editor has no Type or Attach To Field column; those belong to the separate /rules editor.

title: Search, view and export Rules and Expressions
prerequisites: An authenticated session accepted by the rules guard.
Rule group and rule lookup services available.
steps: Open /rules/rules-list.
Choose Select Rule Group, using All to load all rules.
Enter Search text to filter RuleName, Expression or Result in the loaded rows.
Review group/rule descriptions, Expression, Result, Execution Order and Is Active.
Use View or Edit on the intended row, or Add New for a new rule.
Use Export as Excel to export the rendered table to an Excel workbook.
notes: Export uses the rendered table, so search-filtered visible rows are the relevant source, not a separate backend full-dataset export.
The generated filename is epltable.xlsx.
View/Edit/Add New pass group ID, rule ID and edit mode via browser navigation state; a cold detail URL is not equivalent.
The template exposes these actions directly even though the component also reads action permissions; do not treat their visibility as proof of backend authorization.

title: Create or edit rule metadata and error type
prerequisites: Open Add New or Edit from Rules and Expressions.
A configured rule group.
steps: Select Rule Group in the Rule section.
Enter a nonblank Rule Name, Rule Description and ExecOrder.
Choose Type from General, MedicalError or TechnicalError, and set Active.
Complete Rule Expressions and Results before saving.
Use Save, inspect the returned message and reopen the rule from the list to verify the change.
notes: Rule name, description, execution order and Type have required validators; execution order and Type initialize to 1.
Save explicitly rejects a missing group or name and whitespace-only name.
The save handler navigates to the list after receiving either a success or a failure Status. Navigation alone is not proof that the rule was saved.
An eye-opened View disables the main form; this is distinct from editing.
No rule execution/test-preview button is verified on this screen.

title: Build multi-row rule expressions with conditions and brackets
prerequisites: An editable rule with its group selected.
Applicable fields and user-function lookups returned by the rule services.
steps: In the first Rule Expressions row, choose Field, Operator and Value.
Use a returned user function instead of a field only when that is the intended expression, using the row's UserFunc switch.
Use the Arithmetic choices +, -, * or / and value chips only when needed; review the generated Expression below the grid.
Select AND or OR in Condition before using the plus action to append the next expression.
Add brackets with the ( ) controls where needed and ensure opening and closing counts match.
Remove unwanted extra rows with the row remove action, leaving at least one expression, then save the complete rule.
notes: Field, Operator and Value carry required validators.
Offered comparisons include Equal, NotEqual, LessThan, LessThanOrEqualTo, GreaterThan, GreaterThanOrEqualTo, Contains, NotContains, RegularExp and the four Character comparison variants.
Adding a row without an AND/OR selection shows 'Kindly select AND/OR before adding'. The final single row cannot be deleted.
Field names, functions and special value choices are configuration-dependent; do not invent domain fields.
Balanced bracket counts are checked, but do not alone prove full expression semantics or runtime validity.

title: Resolve regular-expression and bracket save warnings
prerequisites: A rule opened in its correct editor with edit access.
steps: If 'please correct RegEx in Line no' appears, locate the indicated expression row and review the value supplied with RegularExp.
Correct the regular expression and trigger the editor's normal change handling before trying Save again.
If an open/closed-bracket warning appears, compare the ( ) selections across all expression rows and correct missing or surplus parentheses.
Confirm the group and a nonblank rule name are populated, then retry Save.
Inspect the returned message and reopen the saved rule rather than treating a route change as proof of success.
notes: Both editors maintain a regular-expression-valid flag and count expression brackets before sending the save request.
The source does not establish a full server-side syntax test or guarantee that a rule with balanced counts evaluates as intended.
Do not test a rule with live healthcare records in AI requests; use approved synthetic test data in an authorized environment.

title: Attach a rule result to a field and set its message and severity
prerequisites: An editable /rules/manage-rule form with group fields loaded.
steps: In Results, select Attach To Field from the rule group's available field names.
Enter Description and Message.
Select Severity Level from the returned lookup.
Choose Severity Category as Both, Technical or Medical.
Use the result-row plus/remove controls for additional outcomes as needed, retaining at least one result.
Save the complete rule and reopen it to verify the field attachment and message.
notes: Attach To Field maps to ResultField, Description to ResultName and Message to ResultValue; these and both severity controls have required validators.
Severity ID and category initialize to 2, but the severity name for an ID depends on the service lookup; do not assume a hardcoded severity label.
Severity Category is separate from the rule-level Type.
The settings editor uses Result Name and Result Value instead and has no Attach To Field control.

title: Find tasks by date, facility, payer, manager, supervisor or status
prerequisites: Authenticated task access and appropriate configured task actions.
steps: Open /task/task-list.
Set From Date and To Date, and optionally Facility, Payer, Manager, Supervisor and Status.
Choose Status from Pending, Under Process or Completed when needed.
Use Search and review Task Id, Task Name, facility/payer, dates, technical/medical supervisor and manager, and status.
Use the row's View or Edit action for the selected task.
Use Reset to clear the search according to the screen defaults.
notes: If From Date exceeds To Date, the component moves To Date to From Date.
Date-only searches and searches with other filters use different task-service methods; choose explicit filters rather than assuming a global unfiltered list.
List search/page state is saved before navigating to the detail screen and restored on return.

No task backend implementation was found in the supplied Cyclus.Claim scope for the separate TaskManagement service routes; task business constraints below are verified at the current UI/service-contract level.

title: Create a technical or medical review task
prerequisites: Use Add New from the task list so taskId navigation state is supplied.
Configured facilities, payers, managers, supervisors and reviewer teams.
Technical Review and/or Medical Review action permission to display the corresponding section.
steps: Use Add New on Tasks.
Set From Date and To Date, select Facility and Payer, and choose Encounter Type as appropriate from Outpatient or Inpatient.
Review the generated Task Name, based on facility alias, month/year and payer; the template presents the name as disabled.
In each applicable Technical or Medical section, select its manager and supervisor to load the team.
Set a positive percentage for at least one intended reviewer, and set Claim Type for every reviewer with a positive percentage: All, Priority or Non Priority.
Use Save and inspect the result before checking the task in the list.
notes: The save handler requires task name, facility and payer. Selecting a manager requires its corresponding supervisor.
An active manager/supervisor section requires at least one positive-percentage reviewer. At least one technical or medical reviewer with positive percentage is required overall.
The inspected handler does not establish a total-percentage-equals-100 requirement; do not invent one.
From/To dates have required form validators. The hidden Is Repetitive checkbox is not a verified user-facing recurrence workflow.

A successful save returns to the task list. The explicit assignTask call following save is commented out, so do not promise that saving immediately allocates claims. Downstream allocation and backend enforcement are unverified in the supplied backend scope.

title: Edit task staffing and choose current-month or future-task scope
keywords: Yes, Apply to All Future Tasks
prerequisites: An existing task opened through Edit, not View.
Authorized understanding of the affected task's facility, payer, encounter type and management hierarchy.
steps: Open the task's Edit action from Tasks.
Review the task identity and current Technical/Medical team.
Modify intended staffing percentages, claim types or other editable relevant settings, retaining required reviewer/supervisor combinations.
Use Save.
If Apply Changes appears, choose 'Yes, Apply to All Future Tasks' for the broader scope, or 'No, Current Month Only' for the narrower scope.
Review the returned result and inspect affected tasks after saving.
notes: The prompt is conditional on an existing edited task and detected relevant changes; it is not shown for every save.
The prompt describes future matching by Facility, Payer, Encounter Type, Technical/Medical Manager and Technical/Medical Supervisor.
The code sets ApplyToFutureTasks from the choice. The separate TaskManagement backend implementation is outside the supplied backend scope, so exact backend matching/execution is unverified.
Facility, Payer and Encounter Type are read-only in edit/view templates; date controls are also programmatically disabled in the existing-task path.
View mode disables Save and is not an edit entry path.

title: Add a reviewer to an existing task team
prerequisites: An existing task in Edit mode with the intended Technical or Medical section visible.
A supervisor whose available users can be loaded.
steps: Use the plus control titled Add new Team member in the intended Technical or Medical section.
In Select Users To Add, select an available member.
Use Add Member.
If 'Select A Member' or 'Member Already Exists' appears, correct the choice rather than adding a duplicate.
Review the added member's percentage and Claim Type in Team, adjust as intended, then Save the task.
If prompted about future tasks, choose the intended save scope and verify the result.
notes: The member popup is shown for an existing task; its plus control is disabled in View mode.
The current add-member object initializes percentage to 100 and ClaimType to All; review these defaults rather than assuming they match the intended allocation.
Adding a member to the local team is not by itself proof of a persisted task update.

title: Remove a task member from this task or matching future tasks
prerequisites: An existing task in Edit mode and an intended member selected for removal.
Authority to alter the task staffing scope.
steps: Use the intended team member's delete/remove control.
Read Delete Member carefully.
Choose This Task Only for a single-task deletion, or This and All Future Tasks for the broader matching scope.
To abort, dismiss the dialog with its close/outside dismissal rather than selecting the button labelled This and All Future Tasks.
Wait for the deletion response and verify the member is removed from the appropriate task team.
Ensure remaining staffing still meets the task's reviewer and supervisor constraints.
notes: Unusually, the dialog's cancel-style button means 'This and All Future Tasks' and sends applyToFutureTasks=true; it is not a no-change Cancel action.
The dialog describes matching Facility, Payer, Encounter Type, Manager and Supervisor.
For existing tasks, removal calls deleteMember immediately; it is not merely a local unsaved grid edit. For a new unsaved task it only removes locally.
Exact backend propagation and claim-reassignment consequences are not verified in the provided TaskManagement backend scope.

title: Use the task list's delete action deliberately
keywords: Do You Want To Delete Task
prerequisites: Task-list access with the row delete action available.
The correct task identified by Task Id, facility, payer and dates.
steps: Find the intended task in Tasks.
Use its delete action and review 'Do You Want To Delete Task ?'.
Choose Yes! only when the deletion/deactivation is intended; otherwise cancel.
Review the response and refreshed task list.
notes: The frontend sends TaskId with IsActive=false through updateTask; this is an inactivation-style request, not verified physical deletion.
The component refreshes on a successful result and displays an error on failure.
Removal of assignments, retention of history and recovery/reactivation behavior are not established by this UI action.

title: Search Task Assignments and interpret assignment counts
prerequisites: Task-assignment access and available task/user/facility lookup data.
steps: Open /task/task-assignments and open the Search panel.
Set Task Id or Task Name, User, Role, Facility, Payer, Supervisor, Status and From Date/To Date as needed.
Use Search.
Review Task Id, Task Name, User Name, Role, Encounter Type, supervisors/managers, priority counts, Completed, Total Claims and Status.
Scroll the assignment list for additional pages where available; use the relevant row controls to inspect or reassign work.
notes: A positive typed Task Id overrides the Task Name selection in the request.
Initial search dates are current-month dates; when dates are cleared, the request falls back to previous-month boundaries.
A missing facility selection is sent as facilityId=1 by the current component, not necessarily 'all facilities'. Select the intended facility explicitly.
The UI's priority-column captions are not sufficient to invent business definitions beyond the returned Priority/NonPriority counts.
Backend assignment visibility and status transitions are not verified outside the current UI/service contract.

title: Inspect an assignment and redistribute its work
prerequisites: The intended assignment opened in Task Re-Assignment.
Applicable assignment controls available for the current role/configuration.
steps: Open the assignment's detail/reassignment panel.
Confirm the displayed task/user, date range, Facility, Payer and technical/medical management context.
Inspect Assigned Claims before altering allocation.
Use Assign to load available reassignment users and select intended recipients in Select Users To Distribute when offered.
For the Re-Distribute path, read 'Do You Want To Distribute Task ?' and choose Yes! only if redistribution is intended.
Inspect the response and refreshed Task Assignments list.
notes: The explicit redistribute path clears the local recipient array before sending reAssignTask; it must not be described as guaranteed allocation to a manually selected subset.
The Assign recipient path rejects proceeding without a selected user.
UI/server behavior when no reassignment-user list is returned is conditional: the component can fall back to distribution.
The current component does not establish a complete allocation algorithm, equal-share guarantee, or 100% sum rule.

title: Reassign available claims from selected task assignments
prerequisites: Task-assignment access with selection/reassignment controls enabled.
Search results containing reassignable Priority or NonPriority claims.
steps: Search the intended assignment date range and scope.
Select the assignment rows to move, reviewing task/user identity and claim counts.
Use Re-Assign Task Claims.
If 'There are no claims available to ReAssign!' appears, review the selected rows and counts instead of retrying an empty selection.
Choose one or more recipient users in the popup and use Assign Claims.
Review the response and reloaded assignments; selections are cleared after the request completes.
notes: The request carries recipient IDs, selected task/user/count objects and the search FromDate/ToDate.
Assign Claims rejects an empty recipient selection.
The header selection control works over the currently loaded assignment list, not a proven server-wide selection of every matching page.
The code's user-filter enablement condition is permissive; visible controls alone do not prove a specific user-selection restriction.
Completed-claim movement and the server's allocation algorithm are not verified by these client sources.

title: View a task's reassignment history
prerequisites: A task assignment with View Log available.
steps: Find the intended task assignment and choose View Log.
In Reassignment History, inspect Assigned To, Total Claims, Assigned On and Reassigned By.
Use Previous or Next to move through history pages when enabled.
Use Close to return to assignments.
notes: History is requested by task ID, starting at page 1 with page size 10.
No records or a failed lookup must not be represented as proof that no reassignment ever occurred.
Do not copy actual staff identifiers or history records into AI prompts.

title: Choose the workflow mapping screens without confusing duplicate routes
prerequisites: Authenticated workflow access and configured menu entries.
steps: For module/screen-to-workflow mapping, use /workflowmanagement/workflow-mapping-list and its Create New Mapping action.
For a workflow definition list/editor referenced as /workflowmanagement/workflow and /workflowmanagement/manageworkflow, first verify that the target deployment actually resolves the intended screen.
If the definition routes redirect, fail or load a different screen, report the duplicate lazy-route configuration instead of repeatedly changing mappings.
Open an existing definition through its list action when reachable because the editor requires history state.
notes: The root route table declares workflowmanagement twice. The components/workflowmanagement module is first and has new-mapping/workflow-mapping-list children; components/workflow-management is second and declares workflow/manageworkflow.

Angular routing tries configurations in order, so the first mount has priority. Its empty child redirect omits pathMatch:'full', further complicating deep-link recognition/fallback. Source order does not prove that both definition routes are reachable in the running deployment.
Definition instructions in this knowledge are explicitly route/configuration conditional, not a claim that both modules are simultaneously accessible.

The components/workflow-management/workflow-mapping component is not a declared leaf route here and contains static placeholder markup; no extra route or working configuration workflow is invented for it.

title: Search module and screen workflow mappings
prerequisites: Access to the first-priority workflowmapping module and its lookup services.
steps: Open /workflowmanagement/workflow-mapping-list.
Optionally choose Module Name and WorkFlow, then use Search.
Review Module Name, Screen Name, WorkFlow Name, Created On and Status in List of WorkFlow Names.
Use the row pencil action to edit a mapping or Create New Mapping to add one.
notes: Search sends the selected ModuleId and WorkflowId; it also runs after the search component initializes.
Status displays Active or InActive from the returned mapping Status.
The list has no verified delete or status-toggle action; only a pencil action is present.
The duplicate workflowmanagement root mounts remain a routing caveat; this mapping module is declared first.

title: Map a module screen to a workflow
prerequisites: An existing workflow definition available in the lookup.
A configured module and screen and access to the mapping form.
steps: Use Create New Mapping from the mapping list, or the existing row's pencil action.
Select Module Name; this loads its Screen Name choices and clears the previous screen.
Select Screen Name and WorkFlow Name.
Use Add Workflow for a new mapping or Update Workflow when editing.
Use Back or Cancel to return without requesting a save.
After saving, reload the mapping list and verify the module/screen/workflow combination.
notes: Module, Screen and WorkFlowName have required validators, and the submit button is disabled while invalid or loading; the save handler itself does not independently check form.valid before constructing the payload.
Edit mode is selected by the workflowid query parameter supplied by the list, representing the mapping record ID, not necessarily the workflow-definition ID.
The save callback displays a success message and navigates to the list without inspecting a business Status flag. Verify stored data instead of treating the toast alone as proof.
No duplicate mapping, uniqueness or active-status validation is established in the inspected mapping service; do not promise those constraints.
The related backend mapping service delegates add/update to the repository; workflow-level authorization and execution outcomes must be verified separately.

title: Browse workflow definitions when the definition routes resolve
prerequisites: Deployment routing verified to reach the second workflow-management module despite its duplicate root mount.
Authorized access to workflow definitions.
steps: Only after verifying route resolution, open /workflowmanagement/workflow.
Enter part of the workflow name in Search ... to filter names case-insensitively.
Review the displayed Sequence ID, Name, Description and Status; use Previous, page numbers or Next for the filtered list.
Use View for inspection or Edit for a change; these actions pass workflow ID and edit mode to the definition editor.
Use Add Workflow to start a new definition.
If the route does not resolve as expected, stop and report the duplicate root-route issue rather than assuming the list is empty.
notes: This is conditional source coverage of declared routes, not verified runtime reachability.
The root mounts components/workflowmanagement before components/workflow-management.
The component uses a client-side filtered list with a page size of 10.
List/get-by-ID backend operations use the current organization context.

title: Create workflow levels and approval type when the editor is reachable
prerequisites: Definition-route reachability verified; the second duplicate workflowmanagement mount is conditional.
Editor opened using Add Workflow or Edit from the definition list.
Users or roles available for later step configuration.
steps: Enter Workflow Name and optionally Description; set Active as intended.
Use Add Level.
Enter Level Name, select User Approve Type as Either or All, and set Is Active.
Use Add Level or Edit Level in the dialog as appropriate.
Add at least one user step to every created level before saving.
Use Save Workflow and review the returned result; success navigates to the definition list.
notes: Workflow Name is required and limited to 250 characters; Description is limited to 500.
The level form requires StageName and has required validators on approval type and active-state controls.
Save warns 'The level should contains at least one user' when any existing level has no step. The inspected check does not require that at least one level exists.
Either/All are exposed approval-type choices; the full engine progression semantics are not established by the editor alone.

Important backend discrepancy: WorkflowService.MapWorkflowDTO and MapDetailDTO force workflow and level active flags to true. Unchecking Active in this form is not proven to persist an inactive definition/level.

title: Add user or role-derived approver steps to a workflow level
prerequisites: A reachable editable workflow definition with a level created.
Configured users/roles and authorized access to choose approvers.
steps: On the intended level, open Add Step.
Choose the user-based Step Type and Select User entries, or choose Role and Select Role.
For a role-based step, wait for the role's user lookup before adding.
Use Add Step and review the resulting users under that level.
Remove unintended steps or levels with the displayed remove controls.
Ensure every retained level has at least one user and use Save Workflow.
notes: Role selection is expanded into users at edit time: the component fetches users by the selected role and appends one step per returned user. It is not evidence of a live dynamic role membership reference at approval time.
The component does not establish duplicate-approver prevention or mandatory selection validators for Users/Roles; choose valid entries before adding.
Although one-user restriction code exists, it is commented out; do not claim Either levels permit only one user.
Route reachability is conditional because the definition module is the second duplicate workflowmanagement lazy mount.
Backend mapping initializes each saved user step to the None approval status and active=true; runtime approval history is separate from definition editing.

title: Resolve a duplicate rule-name rejection without creating another rule
prerequisites: An attempted new-rule save and permission to inspect the relevant rule group.
steps: Read the save response rather than assuming that returning to a list means success.
If the response says that the RuleName already exists, return to the correct rules list and select the intended group.
Search for the existing rule by name and inspect its Expression and Result.
Use Edit on that existing rule if the intent is to change it.
If a genuinely different rule is required, use a distinct nonblank name in the intended group and complete expressions/results before saving.
Reopen the intended record after the response to verify persistence.
notes: The inspected payer RuleMasterRepository checks duplicate names only on add when RuleId is zero.
The duplicate comparison trims the name and compares it case-insensitively within the same RuleGroupId; changing only letter case or surrounding spaces does not make a new name.
This add-mode check does not prove equivalent duplicate enforcement during rename/edit.

The related RuleMaster save endpoint requires Rule New or Edit permission, while several field/function/severity lookup endpoints require Rule View. Route access or a visible button alone is not sufficient proof of backend permission.

title: Print or export the displayed workflow-definition page
prerequisites: Verified runtime access to the second workflow-management module despite the duplicate root mount.
The intended workflow-definition page loaded and authority to export its configuration.
steps: Open the reachable workflow-definition list.
Use Search ... and the paging controls to display the intended workflow definitions.
Use Print to open the browser print workflow.
Use Export to generate the workbook from the displayed table.
Review the downloaded workbook, named WorkflowExcelSheet.xlsx, and keep exported configuration within approved storage.
notes: Export reads the rendered excel-table HTML element, whose rows are the current page's items. It is not a verified export of every server-side definition or every filtered page.
Print calls window.print; print-dialog completion is browser-dependent.
These are conditional source-verified actions; the duplicate workflowmanagement root route prevents claiming unconditional runtime reachability.
The separate static workflow-mapping placeholder component is not the source of this export workflow.

title: Open and review a workflow approval-link request
prerequisites: An authorized workflow request link containing token and refid query values.
Do not supply or expose real token values to an AI assistant.
steps: Open the issued link as provided; the application uses the #/workflow-status route with token and refid query values.
Review Request ID and Request Description and confirm that the request is the one you are authorized to act on.
Review the displayed reconciliation summary and approval-level/user status history.
Only after review, enter Comments if needed and choose the intended approval action.
If the page reports 'Content Not Found / Already Processed', request verification of the issued link/request state rather than constructing token values manually.
notes: The route is outside the normal layout and has no AuthGuard in the root routing table. The backend validates the token and reference relationship; this is not an unrestricted public approval workflow.
The inspected backend details service currently retrieves payment-reconciliation details, so do not describe this page as a generic viewer for every business module.
The UI passes token and refid as query values. Tokens are secrets and should never appear in knowledge examples, copied links or logs supplied to AI.
HTTP-error handlers do not consistently set a visible failure message; a blank or stale page is not proof of success or an empty request.

title: Approve or reject a workflow request and interpret the outcome
prerequisites: A valid issued request link whose details are loaded.
Authority to decide the displayed request; actual transaction details must remain private.
steps: Review the request summary and approval history before choosing a decision.
Enter Comments when context is needed; the inspected form does not make comments required.
Choose Approve to submit acceptance or Reject to submit rejection.
Read the notification: true response Status produces 'Content Approved Successfully' or 'Content Rejected Successfully'; a false Status produces 'Content Not Found / Already Processed'.

After a handled response, the action buttons disappear. Verify the business workflow's subsequent state through its authorized owner rather than assuming this individual response completed the whole workflow.
notes: The component sends IsAccepted=true for Approve and false for Reject together with remarks and the issued token/reference.
Backend processing validates the user/token and transaction, deactivates the previous user/transaction log and writes a new accepted/rejected user log and transaction log.
A successful individual decision is not proof that all levels are completed, a payment has been released, or a downstream action has occurred.
The shared 'Content Not Found / Already Processed' message is not a precise diagnosis of token expiry versus previously processed versus missing content.
No verified undo/reopen button exists on this screen; do not advise repeated submission as a recovery mechanism.
